title: Matching years reduced the Laptev Sea ice-return forecast gain from 43% to 12% in a 1979-2025 record
abstract: We tested how missing threshold crossings affect a regional sea ice forecast comparison. We used Sea Ice Index Version 4 daily regional extent for 1979-2025. Each forecast used only earlier years. The base model used year. The added model also used the retreat date known by August 31. In the Laptev Sea, the 70% winter-reference threshold gave a 43.4% reduction in mean squared error over 27 tests in 1999-2025. When the 50% and 70% thresholds used the same training and test years, the 70% gain fell to 12.5% over 15 tests in 2011-2025. Its conditional 95% block interval was -73.0% to 52.7%. The 50% gain was 6.0%. In the Kara Sea, matched gains were 43.8% and 42.4%. These results show that threshold score comparisons can change when the year sample is held fixed. They do not prove a physical change in ice recovery or that all of the Laptev difference comes from sample choice. The common-year check was added after initial scores. Short records, selected crossing years, trend assumptions and final data versions limit the result. Code, daily input, source hashes, all forecasts, coverage tables and a numerical audit are included.
